3.text: Another taboo of the Asiatic Eskimo forbids long migratory journeys with

4.text: household and family, to be performed on dog-sledges. Such journeys must be

5.text: performed exclusively in summer-time and with the large skin boat of the family.

6.text: Still another taboo existing among the Asiatic Eskimo refers to the boats

7.text: going to the open sea for hunting sea-mammals. They are forbidden to take

8.text: with them provisions and fresh water, and especially fuel for cooking. Indeed,

9.text: to make a fire in a boat in the open sea is considered as a grave trespass

10.text: against the hunting-chance of the party. The hunters, therefore, can assuage

11.text: their thirst only by sucking sea-ice, when pieces of a proper quality can be

12.text: found, or by swallowing the viscous fluid from the intestines of walrus or

14.text: For provisions, the hunters usually take only raw or dried meat. To

15.text: take along cold cooked meat is permitted only after the coming of puffins,

16.text: which for this reason are often called simply the “cooked.” To cook a meal

22.text: I cannot say what may be the cause of this strange taboo. The natives

23.text: themselves are conscious that it seriously hampers their hunting-expeditions,

24.text: since it makes it impossible for them to go far out to sea. They say, however,

25.text: that the Sea-Being instituted this taboo through his care for the people, lest

26.text: too many of them perish in the open sea. The Sea-Being gave to the Maritime

27.text: people an explicit command not to venture out in the open sea beyond the

28.text: limit where the line of the shore-hills could be seen, and for further security

30.text: The arctic Chukchee, however, have no such taboo. They take with

31.text: them cooked meat, water, fuel for fire, skins, and covering for their beds.

32.text: While in the open sea, they make a fire in the boat on a large piece of sod

33.text: or on a flat box filled with sand, and cook their meat on that improvised

34.text: hearth. Therefore they are able to go out into the open sea far beyond the

35.text: limit of sight of the shore-hills. There they eat and sleep, and often stay

36.text: for two or three days, which, of course, gives them more chance for hunting.

37.text: For their return they rely on the north wind, which blows there frequently,

38.text: and brings their boats in toward the shore.
